গণপ্রজাতন্ত্রী বাংলাদেশ সরকার
অর্থ মন্ত্রণালয়
অভ্যন্তরীণ সম্পদ বিভাগ
(কাস্টমস ও মূল্য সংযোজন কর)

প্রজ্ঞাপন

তারিখ, ১ আষাঢ়, ১৪২২ বঙ্গাব্দ/১ জুলাই, ২০১৫ খ্রিস্টাব্দ

National Board of Revenue: The Ministry of Finance and Internal Resources Division oversees customs and value added tax matters under the regulatory authority of the government.

Customs Act 1969: Under Section 19(1) of this Act, the government, in consultation with the National Board of Revenue, grants duty and tax exemptions on imported goods used for the development of economic zones.
Value Added Tax Act 1991: This Act is cited as a legal basis, read in conjunction with the Customs Act, for providing tax exemptions on imported goods required for economic zone development.
Bangladesh Economic Zones Act 2010: This Act provides the regulatory framework under which developers are appointed and authorized to carry out development activities in designated economic zones.
Economic Zone Developer: Developers appointed under the Bangladesh Economic Zones Act are eligible for exemptions on import duties, regulatory duties, supplementary duties, and value-added tax for goods used in zone development, provided they are registered for value-added tax.
The developer must obtain certification from the Bangladesh Economic Zones Authority for the specific description, quantity, and details of the imported goods to qualify for these tax benefits.

Exemptions do not apply to goods not directly related to development or construction, such as office equipment, appliances, or vehicles, nor to locally available construction materials like cement and steel products.
National Board of Revenue: The government exercises its exemption powers under the relevant tax laws in consultation with this body.
Bangladesh Economic Zones Authority: This authority is responsible for reviewing, approving, and certifying the list of goods imported by developers to ensure they meet the criteria for tax exemption.
Customs Duty: These duties are exempted for goods imported by economic zone developers, subject to strict compliance with specified terms and conditions.
Regulatory Duty: This duty is waived for eligible goods imported by authorized economic zone developers for development purposes.
Supplementary Duty: Authorized developers are exempt from paying this duty on imported goods utilized in the development of economic zones.
Value Added Tax: Exemption from this tax is granted to economic zone developers for imported construction and development goods, conditional upon the developer holding a valid registration.
